samples.summary: fpProfile's `stated_severity` axis is only asserted to EXIST — no fixture distinguishes it from the annotator axis, so reading the wrong severity would pass
samples.evidence: The module makes a point (`validity.mjs:660-667`) that the two severities "must never be confused": `annotator_severity` reads `row.label.severity`, `stated_severity` reads `row.claim?.severity`. The only assertion on that axis is `assert.ok(result.fp_profile.some((g) => g.axis === "stated_severity"))` (validity.test.mjs:512). In that fixture the label severity equals the record severity (`labels = records.map((r,i) => label({... severity: stated[i] ...}))`, line 494), and `pilotCodeRabbitArm`'s default is `annotatorSeverity = (stated) => stated` (line 112), so no test anywhere has annotator ≠ stated for the profile. If `stated_severity`'s accessor were changed to `row.label.severity` (or to a constant `"claim-unavailable"` for the axis label check only), every test in the file would still pass. The severity-weighted-precision test (line 408) does construct a distinguishing fixture — the FP profile has no equivalent. Also untested: the `claim-unavailable` fallback branch (validity.mjs:667).
searchedFor: read pilotCodeRabbitArm and the fp profile test fixtures

samples.summary: The `weights` operator-override path of scoreValidity is never exercised: no test passes a custom weight vector
samples.evidence: `scoreValidity` accepts `weights` and, when non-null, validates it (`assertSeverityWeights(weights)`, validity.mjs:739), threads it into every `precisionCell` as `weightVector`, and stamps `severity_weights_source: "operator override"` (line 914). Grepping the test file for `weights:` / `operator override` finds only min_n's override (lines 620, 625) — no test calls `scoreValidity({ weights: ... })` or `precisionCell({ weights: ... })` with a non-default vector. So the documented "anyone who disagrees can re-run with their own" behaviour (validity.mjs:211-213), the validation of a caller-supplied vector, the propagation of it into the weighted sums, and the `severity_weights_source` string are all uncovered — a bug that ignored `weights` and silently used SEVERITY_WEIGHTS would pass the suite. `assertSeverityWeights` is tested only in isolation.

samples.summary: The `noneJoined` reason — the sentence that explains a zero denominator caused by the JOIN rather than by missing labels — is never asserted
samples.evidence: validity.mjs:837-840 builds a specific reason ("N tier label(s) exist ... and none of them joined the claim population supplied") and passes it as the cell `reason` for both whole-arm cells. The test that reaches this state ("a label carrying a parser vintage with no current vintage...", validity.test.mjs:237) asserts only `join.counts` and `labelled_findings === 0` plus `parse_vintage.basis`; no test asserts the cell's `reason` in that state. Since the docblock claims this is what makes the failure "visible rather than absent" at the metric level, a wrong or missing reason string here would ship unnoticed.
searchedFor: grep 'none of them joined' in validity.test.mjs

samples.summary: relativeRecallBand's "nothing judged real on either arm" branch is untested
samples.evidence: validity.mjs:623-625 returns `not-computed` with a distinct reason when `real + otherReal === 0` while the other arm HAS labels. The relative-recall tests (validity.test.mjs:433, 448, 456, 464) cover reported, otherLabelled===0 and suppressed-union, but none passes `real: 0, otherReal: 0, otherLabelled: >0`. That branch's availability and reason are unexercised.
searchedFor: grep 'union of confirmed defects is empty' in validity.test.mjs

samples.summary: cellLine's `NOT COMPUTED` rendering is never asserted, although the file claims the four states "read differently ON PURPOSE"
samples.evidence: cellLine has four branches (validity.mjs:966-973). The test at validity.test.mjs:195-199 asserts the reported/suppressed/not-measurable renderings; the not-computed line (`NOT COMPUTED — reason`) is never matched. The pending-population test (line 202) checks the payload availability but not the printed line, and `renderReport` is only called on payloads whose zero cells are `not-measurable` (lines 603, 625). So a not-computed cell rendered identically to a suppressed one ("n < min_n") — precisely the confusion the docblock warns about — would pass.
searchedFor: read cellLine and the two renderReport tests

samples.summary: Most caller-error refusals in scoreValidity have no test: unknown arm, unknown label_source, non-object label, non-array labels/unreadable, and mixed populations
samples.evidence: scoreValidity refuses on: non-object label (line 743), unknown `arm` on a label (745), unknown `label_source` (746), unknown `arm` in the `arms` list (759), a non-array `labels`/`unreadable` top-level argument (740-741), and `assertOnePopulation` over mixed populations (763). The test file covers only the item-label schema refusal (line 544), the corpus-version refusal (538), `assertComparableWindow` (549) and a non-array `records` (554). The remaining refusals — several of which are the difference between a wrong figure and an error — are untested.
searchedFor: grep for 'must be one of' / 'not one of' / 'assertOnePopulation' in validity.test.mjs
read all refusal tests in the '--- refusals on caller error' section

samples.summary: The CLI (`main`) is entirely untested: flag validation, --arm choices, the panel --run-id requirement, and the partial→exit 1 contract
samples.evidence: validity.mjs:1045-1161 contains behaviour with its own contracts (`--root`/`--corpus-version` required → exit 2, `--arm` vocabulary, `--min-n` integer check, `--run-id` required for the panel arm, `process.exitCode = complete ? 0 : 1`, and the deliberate use of `repeated()` instead of `parseArgs` for repeatable flags). Nothing in validity.test.mjs imports or spawns the CLI (no `spawnSync`/`execFile`/`main` reference). Noted as minor because sibling scorers follow the same library-only convention (segmentation.test.mjs also has no CLI test), but the repeatable-flag and exit-code contracts are asserted only in prose.
searchedFor: read the CLI section of validity.mjs

samples.summary: Two assertions are tautological against the implementation and cannot fail for the reason their comments claim
samples.evidence: (a) Line 279: `assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(join.counts).sort(), [...JOIN_STATUSES].sort())` — `counts` is built as `Object.fromEntries(JOIN_STATUSES.map(...))` (validity.mjs:433), so this compares JOIN_STATUSES with itself and holds regardless of the join logic. (b) Lines 126-134: the comment claims the vector is proven "DERIVED, not typed" by `assert.deepEqual(KNOWN.map((s) => SEVERITY_WEIGHTS[s]), [4,3,2,1])`, but a hand-typed `{critical:4, major:3, minor:2, nit:1}` satisfies it identically — the test cannot distinguish derived from literal, and the reorder failure it describes can only be observed by mutating KNOWN.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. fpProfile (validity.mjs:664-701) deliberately separates annotator_severity (row.label.severity, line 666) from stated_severity (row.claim?.severity ?? "claim-unavailable", line 667), with a doc block at 660-662 saying the two must never be confused. The only FP-profile test (validity.test.mjs:488-514) builds a fixture where label severity equals record severity (line 494), filters all value assertions to the annotator axis (496-508), and asserts nothing about stated_severity beyond its existence (512). Repo-wide grep shows fp_profile/fpProfile referenced only in validity.mjs and validity.test.mjs, and no other test file imports validity.mjs, so there is no alternate coverage; .trusted has no validity.mjs at all. Every pilotCodeRabbitArm call site uses the default annotatorSeverity = (stated) => stated, so no profile fixture has annotator != stated. The one distinguishing fixture (test:408-429) asserts only result.cells, never fp_profile, even though scoreValidity does compute the profile (validity.mjs:876). The renderReport path prints profile lines (validity.mjs:1012-1017) but the report test (600-614) asserts only cell segments and census text on an identity-severity fixture. "claim-unavailable" appears nowhere outside validity.mjs:667 and is unreachable for joined rows (validity.mjs:431), so that branch is untested too. Swapping stated_severity's accessor to row.label.severity would leave the whole suite green — mutation-insensitive coverage of a documented behavior, major under the missing-tests/vacuous-assertion rubric.

verdict.reason: Verified the absence claim end to end. scoreValidity's operator-override path (validity.mjs:734, 739 -> weights: weightVector at 842/843/864 -> severity_weights_source "operator override" at 914, rendered at 987) has zero test coverage: all ~25 scoreValidity calls and all 4 precisionCell calls in validity.test.mjs (the only test file that imports the module anywhere in the repo) omit `weights`, and the only "operator override" assertions (lines 620, 625) are min_n's. assertSeverityWeights is exercised only in isolation (136-140) and the weighted-precision test (408-429) uses the default vector, so it cannot distinguish weightVector from SEVERITY_WEIGHTS. Searched wide: repo-wide grep for scoreValidity/precisionCell/assertSeverityWeights hits only validity.mjs, validity.test.mjs and non-test .agent-review artifacts; other `weights` hits are metrics.test.mjs's unrelated weightSeverity and .trusted/ copies; the CLI (1142-1153) never passes weights and has no weights flag, so no integration test could reach it. A bug ignoring `weights` would pass the suite — a documented behavior with no meaningful test, blocking under the missing-tests branch of this lens.
